newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan doubtful of imminent progress in Lima crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan doubtful of imminent progress in Lima crisis.

text.p: Japan does not expect a breakthrough in the Peru hostage crisis before the end of the Easter holiday despite recent optimistic media reports, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.

The spokesman told reporters Japan hoped for progress as soon as possible but that media expectations of an end this weekend to the 100-day drama at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima might be overblown.
"Out of hopes for progress, expectations have risen higher than the actual situation merits," the spokesman said.
"We don't expect a major breakthrough will occur during the Easter holidays," the spokesman said. "The Japanese government eagerly hopes that there will be some results after the holidays."
There have been a flurry of Japanese media reports from Lima in the past few days about a possible deal between the Peruvian government and leftist rebels holding 72 hostages.
The Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) seized the ambassador's residence on December 17, initially taking hundreds of captives but later releasing most of them.
The rebels are demanding the release of imprisoned comrades.

The media reports have spoken of a deal which would allow the hostage-takers asylum in another country, possibly Cuba, which has said it would take in the rebels if that would help to end the crisis peacefully.
